subject: Literacy
title: Instruments and body sounds
objectives: Children will copy a short beat with an instrument or their body.
Children will say fast or slow with support.
content: Playing drums and shakers gently, clapping and stamping beats, and fast and slow sounds.
teachingActivities: Play two-beat patterns and wait for children to copy; show fast with quick hands and slow with big gentle hands; model gentle playing and put instruments away together.
learnerActivities: Play drums and shakers, clap and stamp beats, copy a short pattern and say fast or slow.
resources: Shakers made from bottles and rice
A tortoise and a rabbit picture
assessment: Observe whether each child copies a two-beat pattern and plays an instrument gently.

lessons.title: Drums and shakers
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will play a drum and a shaker gently.
successCriteria: Plays a drum with a soft hand
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name familiar animals, make animal sounds and change the loudness of their voices.
resources: Four shakers made from sealed bottles with rice
lessons.starter: Show a drum and say "This is a drum. Boom, boom." Show a shaker and say "This is a shaker. Shh, shh."
teacherActivities: Play the drum with a soft hand and say "Gentle hands." Shake the shaker and name it.
Give each child a shaker and say "Shake, shake, shake" and "Stop".
Pass the drum round the circle so each child plays once.
Say "Put it back in the basket" and collect each instrument.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say "drum" and "shaker".
Children shake and stop on the signal.
Child plays the drum gently and passes it on.
Child puts the instrument in the basket.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play the drum with a soft hand and say "Gentle hands." Shake the shaker and name it. Children: Children watch and say "drum" and "shaker".
Step 2. Teacher: Give each child a shaker and say "Shake, shake, shake" and "Stop". Children: Children shake and stop on the signal.
Step 3. Teacher: Pass the drum round the circle so each child plays once. Children: Child plays the drum gently and passes it on.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Put it back in the basket" and collect each instrument. Children: Child puts the instrument in the basket.

practical.title: Play and stop
steps: Sit in a circle and give everyone a shaker.
Stop the music and everyone holds still.
practical.safety: Check each shaker is sealed with tape and cannot be opened. Keep instruments out of mouths and the volume gentle.

differentiation.support: Hold the shaker with the child and shake together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to be the leader and tell friends when to shake and when to stop.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Names a drum and a shaker
lessons.conclusion: Put the instruments in the basket and say "Drum, shaker, goodbye."
lessons.homeConnection: At home, make a shaker with a sealed bottle and a few beans and shake with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "play a drum and a shaker gently" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Shake, shake, shake your shaker. Stop, stop, stop.

lessons.title: Clap and stamp
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will copy a clap and a stamp.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name familiar animals, make animal sounds and change the loudness of their voices.
resources: A clear space on the mat
lessons.starter: Clap twice and say "Clap, clap." Stamp twice and say "Stamp, stamp." Ask the children to copy.
teacherActivities: Clap once and wait for the children to clap once. Stamp once and wait for them to stamp.
Play a two-beat pattern: clap, clap. Then stamp, stamp.
Let a child choose clap or stamp and lead the group.
learnerActivities: Children copy each action.
Children copy the pattern.
Children copy the mixed pattern with support.
Child leads and the group copies.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Clap once and wait for the children to clap once. Stamp once and wait for them to stamp. Children: Children copy each action.
Step 2. Teacher: Play a two-beat pattern: clap, clap. Then stamp, stamp. Children: Children copy the pattern.
Step 3. Teacher: Mix the actions: clap, stamp. Children: Children copy the mixed pattern with support.
Step 4. Teacher: Let a child choose clap or stamp and lead the group. Children: Child leads and the group copies.

practical.title: Echo clapping
steps: Stand in a circle with room to move.
The teacher plays a short pattern.
practical.safety: Leave space so children do not bump each other. Stamp gently on the floor and stop if anyone is tired.

differentiation.support: Clap with the child’s hands and stamp beside them.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a two-beat pattern for friends to copy.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Copies a clap and a stamp
Copies a two-beat pattern with support
lessons.conclusion: Finish with one big clap and a soft stamp.
lessons.homeConnection: Clap a pattern at home and ask your child to clap it back.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "copy a clap and a stamp" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Fast and slow
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will clap or play fast and slow.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name familiar animals, make animal sounds and change the loudness of their voices.
resources: Pictures of a rabbit and a tortoise
lessons.starter: Show the rabbit and clap fast. Show the tortoise and clap slowly. Say "Fast, slow."
teacherActivities: Tap the drum fast for the rabbit and slow for the tortoise.
Show a card and ask the children to clap fast or slow to match.
Move the scarf fast or slowly and ask the children to move their hands the same way.
Let each child choose a card and play the drum.
learnerActivities: Children watch and listen, then copy with their hands.
Children clap at the right speed.
Children match the scarf speed.
Child plays fast or slow.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Tap the drum fast for the rabbit and slow for the tortoise. Children: Children watch and listen, then copy with their hands.
Step 2. Teacher: Show a card and ask the children to clap fast or slow to match. Children: Children clap at the right speed.
Step 3. Teacher: Move the scarf fast or slowly and ask the children to move their hands the same way. Children: Children match the scarf speed.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child choose a card and play the drum. Children: Child plays fast or slow.

practical.title: Rabbit and tortoise
steps: Place the two pictures on the floor.
Walk fast like a rabbit or slow like a tortoise.
practical.safety: Keep an adult at the front and back and watch that children do not run into each other. Clear the floor first.

differentiation.support: Use one card at a time and move with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say fast or slow and lead the movement.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Is the rabbit fast or slow?

expectedOutcomes: Claps fast and slow on request
Says fast or slow with support
lessons.conclusion: Slow down your clapping until it stops, and whisper "slow".
lessons.homeConnection: Play fast and slow with a spoon on a pot at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "clap or play fast and slow" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Rabbit goes fast, fast, fast. Tortoise goes slow, slow, slow.

lessons.title: Our little band
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will play together in a small band and follow the leader.
successCriteria: Plays an instrument with the group
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name familiar animals, make animal sounds and change the loudness of their voices.
lessons.starter: Wave the scarf and say "I am the band leader. When the scarf goes up, we play. When it goes down, we stop."
teacherActivities: Give each child an instrument. Wave the scarf up and children play, then down and they stop.
Show loud, then quiet with the scarf. Show fast, then slow.
Let two children take turns as the band leader.
learnerActivities: Children play and stop on the signal.
Children change their playing to match.
Leaders hold the scarf and the band follows.
Children play a different instrument.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Give each child an instrument. Wave the scarf up and children play, then down and they stop. Children: Children play and stop on the signal.
Step 2. Teacher: Show loud, then quiet with the scarf. Show fast, then slow. Children: Children change their playing to match.
Step 3. Teacher: Let two children take turns as the band leader. Children: Leaders hold the scarf and the band follows.
Step 4. Teacher: Swap instruments and play again. Children: Children play a different instrument.

practical.title: Little band
steps: The leader waves the scarf up and down.
Swap instruments and leaders after two rounds.
practical.safety: Check that instruments are safe and sealed. Keep the volume gentle and give quiet breaks.

differentiation.support: Sit beside the child and play the same instrument.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to be the band leader and show the group loud or quiet.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do when the scarf goes down?
Can you play with your friends?

expectedOutcomes: Follows the leader to start and stop
lessons.conclusion: Take a bow and put the instruments in the basket.
lessons.homeConnection: Make a band with pots and spoons at home and stop when you say "stop".
teacherReflection: Which children could show "play together in a small band and follow the leader" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 4 rhythm check
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child copies beats and plays an instrument.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name familiar animals, make animal sounds and change the loudness of their voices.
lessons.starter: Play a short beat and say "Can you copy me?" Show the three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: echo clapping, instruments and fast and slow.
Play a two-beat pattern at each station and ask the child to copy it.
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child copies the pattern.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: echo clapping, instruments and fast and slow. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: Play a two-beat pattern at each station and ask the child to copy it. Children: Child copies the pattern.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Rhythm stations
practical.safety: Use sealed shakers and soft drums only. Supervise each station and keep the floor clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one-beat patterns.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to make a pattern for friends to copy.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: copies a two-beat pattern; plays gently; says or shows fast and slow.

questions.question: Is this fast or slow?
questions.expected: Child says or shows the speed.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 4
lessons.conclusion: Take a bow and say goodbye to the instruments.
lessons.homeConnection: Practise clap, clap and stamp, stamp at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child copies beats and plays an instrument" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
